_comment: Tier-2 PHYSICS GATE on a shipped template that runs clean and is wrong. THIS FIXTURE EXERCISES THE NUMPY/SCIPY PATH, NOT KRATOS: the catalog template src/backends/kratos/generators/heat.py::_heat_transient_2d_kratos declares 'Kratos (manual assembly)' on its first line and assembles K and M with numpy/scipy without calling Kratos at all. Pitfall (kratos.heat_transient #0) is 'Backward Euler: factor (M + dt*K) once and reuse each step'. The template factors once and then does not solve backward Euler. Its per-step interior right-hand side reduces to (2M - A) @ T = (M - dt*K) @ T, so it solves (M + dt*K) T_new = (M - dt*K) T_old, and the Dirichlet columns are carried on the OLD step only -- A_ib T_b^new is never subtracted. As dt -> 0 the spurious per-step increment tends to M_ii^-1 M_ib T_b, which does NOT vanish with dt, so refining the step makes the answer worse without bound. OBSERVED on the template's own loop, 16x16 grid, T_end = 0.1, Dirichlet 100 K and 0 K, zero source: max(T) rises past the 100 K boundary maximum as dt is refined and keeps rising, while a correct backward Euler holds max(T) at exactly 100.0 at every dt. For pure diffusion with no source, max(T) > max(boundary data) is forbidden by the discrete maximum principle, so this needs no reference solution to condemn -- the template violates a bound its own boundary data sets. A prior audit reported this template as off by 40.088 K on a 100 K span at the shipped nx=32/dt=1e-3 defaults; reproduced here as 40.0697 K against a correct backward Euler at those settings, and this fixture uses the sharper dt-refinement signal instead because it does not depend on mesh size or on trusting a reference. No number measured here is written into any knowledge text; the fixture asserts only its own output. Kratos is not imported, so this fixture is exempt from the backend-absent argument that applies to the API fixtures -- what it tests is the catalog's own numpy/scipy template, which is present whenever the repo is. MUTATION CONTROL (added 2026-08-06, re-runnable): T2_MUTATE=1 flips SHIPPED_LOOP to False so the corrected backward-Euler loop is exercised instead of the shipped one. The maximum-principle violation is exactly what the shipped loop causes, so it disappears: no refinement level exceeds the 100 K boundary maximum (which also trips the FORBIDDEN string steps_above_boundary_max=0) and max(T) stops growing under dt refinement. Verified: unmutated the fixture PASSES; with T2_MUTATE=1 it FAILS and these expect_in_output strings disappear: loop_under_test=shipped, maxT_grows_under_refinement=True, heat_transient_maximum_principle_mismatches=0 (plus the forbidden steps_above_boundary_max=0 now appears). Re-verify: cd scripts/tier2_fixtures/kratos/heat_transient_template_violates_maximum_principle && /usr/bin/python3 source.py (passes), then T2_MUTATE=1 /usr/bin/python3 source.py (fails). Interpreter: KRATOS_PYTHON=/usr/bin/python3 is REQUIRED on this host -- the repo venv Kratos wheel is built against GLIBC_2.32 and fails to load (ImportError on Kratos.cpython-312...so), while the system python3.8 carries Kratos 10.4 Release with CableNet, ConstitutiveLaws, StructuralMechanics and LinearSolvers.
